intro: To change the cursor style in Visual Studio Code on macOS, you can adjust the settings through the user interface or by editing the configuration file. This allows you to switch between line, block, and underline styles to suit your coding preference.
tldr: Open the Command Palette with Command + Shift + P.
Type cursor style in the search bar.
Select your preferred cursor style from the dropdown menu.
Alternatively, modify the editor.cursorStyle setting in your settings.json file.

blocks.text: Why customize your cursor in VS Code

Your cursor is the most important visual element in your editor. It shows exactly where your next character will appear. Many developers prefer a block cursor because it is easier to see in complex code files. Others prefer a thin line to avoid obscuring characters. VS Code offers six different styles to ensure you can work in a way that feels natural to you.
Changing cursor style via the settings interface
The settings UI is the safest way to change your cursor. It prevents syntax errors that can happen when editing JSON files manually. Follow these steps to find the right setting.

items: Press Command + Shift + P to open the Command Palette.
Type Preferences: Open Settings (UI) and press Return.
Use the search box at the top to find cursor style.
Click the dropdown under Editor: Cursor Style.
Choose between line, block, underline, and thin variants.

blocks.text: If you prefer editing configuration files, you can modify your settings.json directly. This method is faster if you already have the file open. It also allows you to change the cursor color, which is not possible in the standard UI.

items: Open the Command Palette with Command + Shift + P.
Search for Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON) and press Return.
Locate the cursor settings or add new lines to the JSON object.
Save the file with Command + S.

blocks.text: Sometimes your cursor changes even when you did not touch the settings. This is usually due to an extension rather than a configuration bug. The most common culprit is a Vim emulation extension. These extensions change your cursor to indicate different editing modes like normal or visual mode.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor color in VS Code?
faq.answer: Yes, you can change the cursor color by adding a workbench.colorCustomizations object to your settings.json file. You will need to define the editorCursor.foreground property with your desired hex code.

faq.question: Does the cursor style change affect performance?
faq.answer: No, changing the cursor style has no measurable impact on the performance of VS Code. It is a simple visual preference that does not require additional processing power.

faq.question: Why does my cursor keep blinking?
faq.answer: The cursor blinks by default to help you locate it on the screen. You can change this behavior in the settings by searching for Cursor Blinking and selecting solid or another animation style.

steps.text: Press Command + Shift + P on your keyboard to open the Command Palette.

steps.text: Type cursor style in the search bar at the top of the settings tab.

steps.name: Select Cursor Style
steps.text: Click the dropdown menu under Editor: Cursor Style and pick your preferred option.
